evals.expected_output: Agent treats placement as the problem (not routing): flow-based zoning, placement order (mechanicals → anchors → decoupling → TPs), iterate placement with ratsnest as objective, big crossing bundles = move parts now. Offers zone map method.
assertions: response says fix placement before trying to route
response explains flow-based zoning or placement passes

evals.prompt: does it actually matter if my decoupling caps are 5mm from the mcu pins? board is getting tight
evals.expected_output: Agent explains loop inductance physics: ~1 nH/mm rule of thumb, cap impedance dominated by loop not capacitance above ~10 MHz, 5 mm detour + vias defeats the cap exactly where needed; closer beats bigger; suggests opposite-side placement under IC or clearing space by moving other parts; bulk caps lenient.
assertions: response explains loop inductance / frequency-domain reasoning, not a bare rule
response gives a concrete distance target (~1-2 mm class)
response offers a practical alternative (opposite side placement or space clearing)

evals.prompt: wheres the right place for esd protection diodes on my usb port, near the chip or near the connector
evals.expected_output: Agent: at the connector, within mm of entry pads — surge current must take the shortest path to ground before radiating/coupling into interior nets; clamps at the IC protect nothing.
assertions: response says connector side, not IC side
response mentions short path to chassis/board ground

response says keepout extends beyond the antenna region (past module edge)
response advises module/antenna at board edge
